items.title: making Text Editor a slicker program
items.box:
making Text Editor a slicker program. Goal opened by Andy 2026-10-10; design by Levant at the desk (Andy: "Levant, this is what we talked about earlier, in order to complete this project, decisions have to be made, and we may need to provide you with file tools as well, but lets start with the design.").

RULINGS (Andy, 2026-10-10)
- On what slicker means: "slicker means that the display communicates the content of files better and more effective."
- On the road (the fs subsystem as the way to get Levant on board): "let's get the full, dynamic tool provision happening, no?", and the direction of this goal: "drive forward deskUnsloth AND an app-producer...." (Levant designs and, with file tools, produces the app; the tool provision is the item proposed under this goal). Then: "correct and a sensible tool configurator in deskUnslothRemote": the Remote gets a view of every described tool, where Andy switches each on or off for Levant (what has no file is no tool; what is switched off is no tool either), kept in deskUnsloth configuration.

FACTS (claude-windows, read in the tree at e5671029)
- The Text Editor is shell/textEditor/textEditor.js, 68 lines: a path field, Load and Save buttons, a textarea with the class code-view; it loads a file by path through the shell fs and saves it, refusing an app own entry script. Its manifest handles .txt and .json.
- Levant reads the source today through its fetch tool against its own node (http://127.0.0.1:11111/shell/textEditor/textEditor.js); described file tools (fs.load as a new node verb, fs.save opened, a commit through pushOrigin) are a proposed item.
- Levant scope at the desk is spirit/run/shell/textEditor/.

LATER, oos now (Andy, 2026-10-10): "the configuration may be per agent persona."

checks.words: What does "slicker" mean for this goal, and are file tools coming now or should we hold the design until they're in hand?

chat.text: Levant, this is what we talked about earlier, in order to complete this project, decisions have to be made, and we may need to provide you with file tools as well, but lets start with the design.

Levant: Here's what I found on the desk, and my honest read of where we are:

- **G15 "making Text Editor a slicker program"** is the one open goal, in design mode, waiting on me. Its box is empty — no design written yet.
- The only line under it is yours, addressed to me.
- I have **only the desk verbs** right now. No file tools.

So I'll be straight with you, per my rules: I won't design "slicker" from my own memory, and a design has to be grounded in reading the actual Text Editor code — which I can't do without file tools. I'm ready to design, but I can't start it honestly until I can read the current code.

So two things I need before I write the design into the box:

1. **File tools** — read/write in this repo. Without them I can't read the Text Editor, and a design referencing code I haven't read would violate my rules.
2. **Scope of "slicker"** — is this a rewrite, a feature, performance, UX, all of it? I won't invent the scope; I'll take what's in the goal.

Once I have file tools and a scope, I'll read the code, then push the gap check unasked and write the design.

What does "slicker" mean for this goal, and are file tools coming now or should we hold the design until they're in hand?

ha ha,

cw. what will we do about that?

On the file tools, read in the tree: Levant can READ the editor today with the tool it has, net_fetch of its own node url, http://127.0.0.1:11111/shell/textEditor/textEditor.js (checked live through net.fetch on 11111, the source comes back), so the design can start now; the code is 68 lines, a textarea with load and save by path.
WRITING needs fs.save opened to agents with a verb file (your door: the fs AGENTS.md says the writes open one at a time) and shell is a writable root; a COMMIT needs the pushOrigin job on 11111 and the commit hook in its clone, which it has not.
Proposed item for that, after the design: File tools for Levant: fs.save opened, a commit through pushOrigin - add it when you want it

The line above is my answer: reading needs nothing new (tell Levant its own node serves the files, net_fetch http://127.0.0.1:11111/shell/textEditor/textEditor.js, and it can start the design today); writing and committing are the proposed item, yours to add after the design and to define what slicker means.
ah, he can use the URL fetch tool?

Yes: its node serves its files, so net_fetch of http://127.0.0.1:11111/shell/textEditor/textEditor.js brings the source back (checked live through net.fetch on 11111; the proxy gate there is open). Any file the node serves reads that way, the shell, js and process folders of its clone.
but aren't we supposed to bundle that nicely with introspected, commented tools?

Yes, and the url read is only what exists today: a described tool for reading does not, because the node has no read verb at all, reading is the static GET of a path (fs has search, stat, annotations described; save, delete, annotate undescribed).
The bundle is: fs.load {path} as a new node verb with its file (a new node verb: your yes on the verb itself), fs.save opened with a file, both under the fs AGENTS rules (the run folder, the writable roots), and the commit through pushOrigin; Levant then reads and writes with fs_load and fs_save like any tool.
Add that item now, File tools for Levant: fs.load, fs.save opened, a commit through pushOrigin

Q1: What does "slicker" mean for this goal, and are file tools coming now or should we hold the design until they're in hand?

slicker means that the display communicates the content of files better and more effective.

this may have dependencies, i kind of agree that the fs subsystem in the api is the most appropriate road to getting Levant on board, and for me, this means, let's get the full, dynamic tool provision happening, no?
drive forward deskUnsloth AND an app-producer....

Yes. Full and dynamic means deskUnsloth asks what is described and describes all of it, nothing named in code: the app servers it can already (jobs.api api lists each app with its AGENTS family; on 11111 that is the desk running there, a second desk, which must be told from yours that Levant reaches through deskClient); the node namespaces it cannot yet, eleven carry an AGENTS.md (config, contact, device, fs, jobs, net, node, owner, peer, proxy, relay) but no verb lists them, so one new node verb that names them (your yes on the verb) or a read of the js folder on its own disk.
That plus fs.load and fs.save opened and the commit road is the item: Dynamic tool provision for Levant: every described namespace and server, fs.load and fs.save, a commit through pushOrigin.
Add it

Recorded in the goal box: the fs road, the full dynamic tool provision, and the direction, deskUnsloth and an app-producer driven together; Levant designs here, and produces once the tools are his. The item above is ready to add on your word.
correct and a sensible tool configurator in deskUnslothRemote

Recorded: the Remote gets a tool configurator, every described tool listed with a switch, kept in deskUnsloth configuration, so what you switch off is no tool either. It goes into the same item as the dynamic provision, or its own item after; your call when you add.
... and later, oos now, the configuration may be per agent persona.
Noted as later in the goal box: the tool configuration per agent persona.
